operational_states.name: Disconnected (DM)
operational_states.description: Initial / power-up state; secondary responds DM to any command except an acceptable mode-set.

operational_states.name: Initialization (SIM/RIM)
operational_states.description: Optional vendor-specific initialization (e.g. firmware download); entered via SIM command, requested via RIM response.

operational_states.name: Normal Response Mode (NRM)
operational_states.description: Unbalanced; primary polls each secondary; secondary transmits only on poll. Half-duplex friendly.

operational_states.name: Asynchronous Response Mode (ARM)
operational_states.description: Unbalanced; secondary may transmit at any time; primary still owns initialization + error recovery + disconnect.

operational_states.name: Asynchronous Balanced Mode (ABM)
operational_states.description: Balanced; both stations are combined terminals (peer); full-duplex point-to-point.

operational_states.name: Frame-reject (FRMR)
operational_states.description: Unrecoverable error condition; station repeats FRMR until cleared by mode-set or RSET.

fsm_hints_transmitter.name: TX_IDLE
fsm_hints_transmitter.description: Output continuous 1-bits or 0x7E flags; wait for command from upper layer.

fsm_hints_transmitter.name: TX_OPEN_FLAG
fsm_hints_transmitter.description: Drive opening 0x7E flag (suspend bit stuffing for the flag itself).

fsm_hints_transmitter.name: TX_ADDRESS
fsm_hints_transmitter.description: Drive Address octet(s) with bit stuffing engaged.

fsm_hints_transmitter.name: TX_CONTROL
fsm_hints_transmitter.description: Drive Control octet (1 byte normal / 2 bytes extended); encode I/S/U + N(S) + N(R) + P/F.

fsm_hints_transmitter.name: TX_INFO
fsm_hints_transmitter.description: Drive Information octet(s) (only for I, UI, UIH, XID, TEST, SM, FRMR) with bit stuffing engaged.

fsm_hints_transmitter.name: TX_FCS
fsm_hints_transmitter.description: Drive 16-bit CRC-CCITT (or 32-bit CRC-32) over Address+Control+Information with bit stuffing engaged.

fsm_hints_transmitter.name: TX_CLOSE_FLAG
fsm_hints_transmitter.description: Drive closing 0x7E flag; may be shared as next opening flag if back-to-back transmission.

fsm_hints_transmitter.name: TX_ABORT
fsm_hints_transmitter.description: If aborting in-flight frame, drive 7 or more consecutive 1-bits.

fsm_hints_receiver.name: RX_HUNT
fsm_hints_receiver.description: Search for opening 0x7E flag pattern in incoming bit stream.

fsm_hints_receiver.name: RX_FLAG_LOCKED
fsm_hints_receiver.description: Flag found; begin frame de-stuffing (strip 0 after 5 ones).

fsm_hints_receiver.name: RX_ADDRESS
fsm_hints_receiver.description: Collect Address octet(s); if extended addressing, continue while top bit = 0.

fsm_hints_receiver.name: RX_CONTROL
fsm_hints_receiver.description: Collect Control octet(s); decode I/S/U discriminator + N(S)/N(R)/P/F/M-bits.

fsm_hints_receiver.name: RX_INFO
fsm_hints_receiver.description: Collect Information octets (variable length) until closing flag detected.

fsm_hints_receiver.name: RX_FCS_CHECK
fsm_hints_receiver.description: Validate FCS residue; CRC-CCITT residue = 0x1D0F; CRC-32 residue = 0xC704DD7B (or 0 depending on convention).

fsm_hints_receiver.name: RX_ABORT
fsm_hints_receiver.description: On 7+ consecutive 1-bits, abort frame in progress and return to RX_HUNT.

fsm_hints_receiver.name: RX_DELIVER
fsm_hints_receiver.description: On successful FCS, deliver decoded frame (I-frame payload → upper layer; S/U-frame → state machine).

synchronization_rules: Synchronous links — receiver clock is recovered from bit transitions; bit stuffing guarantees a transition every 6 bit times within frame body and every 7 bit times during continuous flag idle.
Asynchronous links — receiver re-syncs per octet via start/stop bits; bit stuffing is replaced by octet stuffing.
Bit stuffing is logically transparent: stuffing and de-stuffing operate on the Address+Control+Information+FCS region only — flags themselves are NEVER stuffed.
Frame boundary: opening flag and closing flag are the SAME 0x7E pattern; they MAY share a single octet between back-to-back frames.
arbitration_rule: No bus arbitration at the protocol layer — HDLC is point-to-point (NRM/ARM unbalanced or ABM balanced) or polled multidrop (SDLC NRM). In SDLC NRM, the primary's poll explicitly grants the secondary permission to transmit (poll token).
anti_deadlock_rule: P/F bit is a single-token mechanism — only one poll/final token may be in flight at a time. If a primary's P-bit response does not arrive within timeout T1, the primary times out and re-sends P. In ABM, each combined station maintains its own independent P/F checkpoint cycle.
exit_from_reset_or_disconnected: On power-up the secondary is in disconnected mode (DM). The primary issues SNRM/SARM/SABM (or SNRME/SARME/SABME for extended numbering); secondary responds UA on acceptance and enters the requested operational mode with N(S)=N(R)=0. RSET command (ABM only) resets receive sequence number to 0 without re-establishing the link.
default_signal_state_when_link_idle: Continuous 1-bits OR continuous 0x7E flag bytes; receiver remains in RX_HUNT.
checkpoint_retransmission_rule: When a station receives a P/F bit, it may assume any unacknowledged frames it had sent before its last P/F transmission will never arrive and so must be retransmitted; this is the core retransmission mechanism that all variants (REJ, SREJ, etc.) merely optimize.

go_back_n_vs_selective.go_back_n: REJ — receiver requests retransmission of N(R) and all subsequent frames; transmitter discards N(S)<N(R) acks and resumes from N(R).
go_back_n_vs_selective.selective_reject: SREJ — receiver requests retransmission of only N(R); transmitter retransmits only the explicitly-requested frame; SREJ is optional (not all variants support it).
